FOREWORD
ThIS Indian Standard was adopted by

the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft finalized by the Pesticides Sectional Committee had been approved by the Food and Agriculture Division Council.

2, 4-D ethyl ester granules are used as weedicides.

2, 4-D ethyl ester granules are generally manufactured to contain 4�5 ethyl ester having 4 percent ( mjm ) of 2, 4-D.

percent (m/m) 2, 4-D

In the preparation of this standard, due consideration has been given to the provisions of the Insecticides Act, 1968 and Rules framed thereunder. However, this standard is subject to the restrictions imposed under these, wherever applicable. Por the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded off in accordance with IS 2 : 1960 'Rules for rounding off numerical values (revised)'. The number of significant places retained in the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard.

IS 13513 : 1992

Indian Standard

2,4-D ETHYL ESTER GRANULES SPECIFICATION
1 SCOPE
This standard prescribes the requirements and the methods of sampling and test for 2, 4-D ethyl ester granules.

3.3 Identity Test
When determined by the method prescribed in Annex A, the retention time of the 2, 4-D ethyl ester extracted from the sample shall be the same as that of reference standard 2, 4-D ethyl ester.

2 REFERENCES
The Indian Standards listed below are necessary adjuncts to this standard:

3.4 Physical
The material shall comply with the physical requirements specified in 3.4.1 to 3.4.4.

IS No. tut� 460 Test sieves: Part 1 Wire cloth ( Part 1 ) : 1985 test sieves ( third revision) 1070 : 1992 Reagent grade water specification ( third revision ) Methods of test for pesticides and their formulation (first revision) 2, 4-D ethyl ester, technical 7233 : 1991 ( second revision ) 8190 Requirement for packing of (Part 1) : 1988 pesticides: Part 1 Liquid pesticides ( second revision) Blank granules 9666 : 1980 2, 4-D ethyl ester Ee ( first 10243 : 1992 revision) 2, 4-D ethyl es ter WP (first 10244 : 1992 revision) Methods for sampling of 10627 : 1983 pesticidal formulations 6940 : 1982

3.4.1 Sieving Requirements

Not less than 97 percent by mass of the product shall pass through a test sieve having a mesh size of the upper declared limit and not more than 5 percent by mass of the product shall pass through a test sieve having a mesh size of lower declared limit when determined by the method described in 12.1 of IS 6940 : 1982. 3.4.1.1 The ratio of lower to upper limit of the sieve sizes given under shall not exceed 1: 3.
3.4.2 Dust
When determined by the method prescribed in 12.1 of IS 6940: 1982 not more than 1-0 percent by mass of the product shall pass through 75-micron IS Sieve {see IS 460 (Part 1) 1985. The material retained on the sieve shall comply with the requirements of 3.5.1.

3 REQUIREMENTS

3.1 CODstituents
3.1.1 The material shall consist of 2, 4-D ethyl ester. technical together with carrier materials conforming to IS 9666 : 1980, stabilizer(s) and other forrnulantrs). 3.1.2 2, 4-D ethyl ester, technical used in the formulation of this material shall conform to IS 7233 : 1991.
3.2 Description The product shall consist of dry, free flowing granules, free from visible extraneous matter and dust except for the amount specified ( lee 3.4.2). It may contain added colouring

3.4.3 Storage Heat Stability
After storage at S4 � 2�C for 24 hours, the product shall continue to comply with the requirements of 3.2, 3.4.1 to 3.4.4, 3.5.1 and 3.5.2.
NOTE - The material need not be subjected to heat stability test if it has crossed half of-the Jklf 1ifc as ascertained from its dates of manufacture and expiry declared 00 the containers,

3.4.4 Moisture Content
When determined by the method prescribed in 4 of IS 6940: 1982 the moisture content shall not exceed 4-0 percent by mass. 1

3.5.1 2, 4-D Content
When determined by the method prescribed in Annex A of IS 10243: 1992 (see 7.1 also) the observed 2, 4-D content, percent (mlm) of any of the samples shall not differ from the declared nominal value bv more than the tolerance limits given below:"

expiry; Batch number; Net mass of the contents; Nominal 2,4-D ethyl ester conten t, percent ( mlm ); and Cautionary notice worded as in the Insecticides Act, 1968 and Rules.

6 SAMPLING
When freshly manufactured material is offered for inspection, representative samples shall be drawn and tested as prescribed in IS 10627: 1983 within 90 days of its manufacture. When the material is offered for inspections after 90 days of its manufacture, sampling shall be done as prescribed in IS 10627 : 1983. However, the criteria for conformity of the material when tested, shall be the limits of tolerances, as applicable over the declared nominal value and given under 3.5.1 of this standard.

3.5.2 Free Acidity
Free acidity (as 2, 4-D) shall not be more than O� 5 percent by mass when determined by the method as given in Annex B of IS 10244: 1'92. The granules should be powdered before test.

7 TESTS
7.1 Tests shall be carried out by the appropriate met hods referred to in 3.3, 3.4.1 to 3.4.4, 3.5.1 and 3.5.2 7.2 Powder and weigh the granules equivalent to 0.5.0�6 g of 2, 4-D into a 500-ml roundbottom flask. Add about 1 g potassium hydroxide pellets, 80 ml of isopropanol 20 ml distilled water, 2 to 3 glass beads and' proceed as described in Annex A of IS 10243 : 1992.

4 PACKING
The material shall be packed according to the requirements given in IS 8190 ( Part 1 ) ~ 1988. 5 MARKING The container shall be securely closed and shall bear legibly and indelibly the following information and any other information as is necessary under the Insecticides Act, 1968 and Rules: a) Name of the material and particle size ( see 3.4.1 ); b) Name of the manufacturer;

7.3 Quality of Reagents
Unless specified otherwise, pure chemicals and d istilJed water (see IS 1070: 1992) shall be employed in tests.
NOTE - 'Pure Chemicals' shall mean chemical. tbat do not contain impurities which effect the results of analysis.

ANNEX A
( Clause 3.3 )
IDENTITY TEST
A-I PROCEDURE Weigh accurately 10 g of the finely ground sample in a clean and dry flask. Add 25 ml acetone and shake well. Allow the solution to settle for 30 minutes. The supernatant liquid is filtered through Whatman No. S or equivalent filter paper. Collect the filtrate which is to be used for gas chromatography by the method prescribed in Annex G of IS 7233 : 1991. .
